source_text: dimitti concupiscentiam carnis in Baptismo, non ut non sit, sed ut in peccatum non imputetur; quamvis autem reatu suo iam soluto, manet tamen dixerim, quo ipsa rea est, eoque soluto illa permaneat absoluta. Quod utique si sensissem, profecto eam malam esse non dicerem, sed fuisse. Ac per hoc, secundum mirabilem intellegentiam tuam, quando audis in aliquo homicidii reatum solutum, non hominem, sed ipsum homicidium a reatu existimas absolutum. Sic intellegat quis, nisi qui non erubescit laudare, cum qua compellitur dimicare? Et quomodo te iactas et exsultas in redarguendo istam sententiam, non meam plane, sed tuam? Talia quippe dicis, qualia dicenda sunt in eos, qui per Baptismum sanctificatam et fidelem factam concupiscentiam carnis affirmant in eis, in quibus regeneratis manet tamen. Sed hoc tibi potius qui eam bonam praedicas, convenit dicere
pass_a_gloss: Dimitti desire of-flesh in in-baptism, not so-that/as not may-be, but so-that/as in sin not imputetur; although however in-guilt his-own already soluto, manet nevertheless i-said, whither herself rea is, eoque soluto that permaneat absoluta. that/which utique if sensissem, profecto her malam to-be not dicerem, but to-have-been. and through this, according-to mirabilem intellegentiam tuam, when audis in aliquo homicidii reatum solutum, not human-being, but itself homicidium from in-guilt existimas absolutum. thus intellegat who, unless who not erubescit laudare, when/with where compellitur dimicare? and how you iactas and exsultas in redarguendo that position, not my plainly, but tuam? such indeed you-say, qualia dicenda are in them, who through Baptismum sanctificatam and fidelem factam desire of-flesh affirmant in to-them, in to-whom regeneratis manet nevertheless. but this to-you rather who her bonam praedicas, convenit to-say.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Augustine reports that Julian attacks his words ‘its liability to guilt has already been removed’ as though Augustine meant that sexual desire itself was released from guilt through baptism.
Of infants Julian and his party say: ‘To their natural good, let the good of sanctification be added.’

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
